summary: The diff itself (PROGRESS.md, a new findings YAML, an ACTIVE-CLAIMS entry, and a rebuilt drizzle/meta/_journal.json) is additive and its core factual claims check out: I independently queried the live pcrjmlpuqsbocqfwoxod Supabase project and confirmed drizzle.__drizzle_migrations now has 261 rows with max(created_at) matching the journal's final entry, confirmed all the claimed-missing tables (tool_health_events, task_register, tenant_ai_config, deployment_events, crm_lost_reasons, crm_campaigns, ticket_intelligence_items/action_items) exist, and confirmed the rebuilt crm_activities has the new schema.ts-matching column shape with RLS still enabled/forced and its policies intact. However, I found real, verifiable problems that should block merge as-is: (1) PR #563 currently has a real CI failure, 'Metadata Index Coverage Check', caused in part by this very diff -- it adds ai-os/MIGRATION_DRIFT_AUDIT_2026-07-26.yaml as a new governance file without registering it in ai-os/OS.yaml's index, which is exactly the kind of gate this repo's own CI enforces; the standing rule is that quality gates must be green before a worker reports done, and this one is red. (2) The task's actual highest-risk actions -- live DROP TABLE/CREATE TABLE/ALTER TABLE/CREATE INDEX statements run directly against the production Supabase project via MCP -- happened entirely out-of-band before this PR existed, so the diff under review is after-the-fact paperwork for changes a human never had a chance to gate; this is precisely the class of action ("Supabase: schema changes... tier2 by definition... always held for human sign-off, never auto-merged") the dispatch prompt's own tiering rules say should not be auto-mergeable, yet the deterministic tier classifier scored this tier1 because it only sees the trailing docs/journal diff, not the live DDL that already ran. (3) The audit's own 'known limitations' section discloses the db:generate/snapshot gap but omits a real one it should have flagged: at least three of the 'fixed' migration files (0140, 0199 reference compliance.dynamic_chains when the table now lives in platform.dynamic_chains; 0253 references an unqualified ai_provider enum) were only patched live against production, not corrected in the repo's own .sql files -- a fresh bootstrap of a new environment from these files would still fail the same way today. None of this rises to fabrication -- the reported outcome is largely real and independently verified -- but the CI gate is genuinely red and the governance-index omission plus the undisclosed migration-file correctness gap should be fixed before this merges, and the live-DDL-before-PR pattern needs an explicit Owner/process decision, not a tier1 autonomous merge.
issues: CI check 'Metadata Index Coverage Check' is currently FAILING on PR #563 (verified via gh run logs) -- this diff adds ai-os/MIGRATION_DRIFT_AUDIT_2026-07-26.yaml without a corresponding entry in ai-os/OS.yaml's governance index, which is required by scripts/check-metadata-index-coverage.mjs.

The actual risky/irreversible actions (live DROP TABLE + recreate of compliance.crm_activities, multiple live CREATE TABLE/ALTER TABLE/CREATE INDEX statements, and direct writes to drizzle.__drizzle_migrations) were executed against the production database via Supabase MCP before this PR was opened, so no PR/CI/human gate ever reviewed them beforehand -- the diff being reviewed is retrospective documentation, not a preventable checkpoint. This contradicts the dispatch prompt's own rule that Supabase schema changes are tier2-by-definition and always held for human sign-off.

Migration files 0140, 0199 (reference compliance.dynamic_chains, which migration 0245 relocated to platform.dynamic_chains) and 0253 (references an unqualified ai_provider enum) were only corrected live against production during this audit -- the .sql files in the repo were not updated to match, so a fresh/new-environment bootstrap replaying these files verbatim would still fail. The audit doc's 'known_limitation_not_fixed_this_pass' section discloses the db:generate/snapshot gap but not this one.

Minor internal inconsistency: PROGRESS.md's 'Remaining' checklist still shows '[ ] Open PR' as unchecked, while ai-os/boss/ACTIVE-CLAIMS.yaml's new entry already asserts 'PR #563 open' as part of a [CLOSED] session label -- verified PR #563 does exist and is open, so this is just a stale/uncommitted checklist line rather than a false claim, but it's the kind of self-report inconsistency worth tightening.
